title: Toronto laneway-suite fire-access generic alternatives (City technical study summary)
code_edition: 2012 Ontario Building Code (edition context stated in the City report); underlying project code edition not applicable

facts.text: Toronto Building and Toronto Fire Services commissioned fire-protection engineering review of ways to address laneway-suite access routes longer than 45 m.
The report records a consultant proposal to allow a route up to 90 m when the apparatus is within 45 m of a hydrant, subject to additional fire-safety measures.

Two described options use either automatic sprinklers with an exterior strobe, or passive exposure/fire-protection measures with an exterior strobe; the report describes examples and conditions rather than a site-specific permit design.

The report says the Chief Building Official and Fire Chief agreed that the consultant proposals should form the basis of a generic alternative solution; a public guide was still being developed at that report date.
Toronto Fire Services is reported to have reduced its clear-path width requirement from 1.0 m to 0.9 m and to allow limited existing protrusions.

limitations: The 10-page City staff report summarizes consultant recommendations; the underlying fire-engineering report and example project drawings are not attached.
The report describes work in progress as of September 2020; later implementation status is not established by this attachment.
The attachment exposes the study recommendation; no individual approval is available.
